title: Testing Instrument Compatibility with Rare Events and Unknown Category Order
banked_reason: The matched three-branch frontier applies only to the engineered rational two-profile library with public blocks and rank sets; its attaining test does not control the unrestricted compatibility null.
gap_reasons: The matched three-branch frontier applies only to the engineered rational two-profile library with public blocks and rank sets; its attaining test does not control the unrestricted compatibility null.
The unrestricted contribution is a K^(1/4) sample-complexity ratio lower bound on the calibrated equal-information surface, leaving the full unknown-order complexity uncharacterized.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched three-regime original-record frontier on a disclosed public two-profile library, supplied-order benchmarks, and a calibrated full-class K^(1/4) order penalty. Math and decision referees passed; the cold referee and independent validity gate rated the delivered contribution incremental below the field floor because engineered-family attainment does not characterize unrestricted unknown-order complexity. Banking stops before Lean formalization; practical calibration, stale prose, and broader-class attainment remain future work, and no theorem is claimed Lean verified.
tldr: Instrumental compatibility can require more information when nominal instrument categories must be ranked from the data. The focal question evaluates the finite-error original-record testing surface of a disclosed rational 64-profile library with unknown within-block assignments across the entire first-stage and rarity rectangle. Its null is exactly compatible and its alternative has fixed positive two-cone distance, while all full marked tensors through degree three agree. The substantive calculation is a fourth-order likelihood bound retaining a rare-channel factor and an original-record variance bound retaining treatment-outcome dependence. Distinct supplied-order library and unrestricted-profile benchmarks then support a polynomial order-uncertainty penalty for the full compatibility class. Family attainment remains restricted to the public library.
gap: Sharp observable IV restrictions and fixed-category contact inference leave the evaluated joint rare-event and order-information benchmark unsettled. Generic permutation-mixture and repeated-record theory already supplies much of the machinery.
fill: The research outputs are an explicit uniformly matched library sample-complexity surface, total finite original-record tests, same-family all-test converses, distinct same-record order benchmarks, and a full-class polynomial penalty on a legal comparison surface.
